quote: it's super it's super annoying the degree to which you guys reach out
stewart_read: This is a protocol-type complaint (procedural, not persuasive) that the rep resolves correctly by action, not argument.
coaching_implication: Good handling — rep should keep resolving contact complaints with immediate corrective action, not with a sales pitch first.

quote: So I'm not gonna give you my utility bill. That's like a Personal document.
stewart_read: This is a trust/privacy objection to bill collection; rep responds by shrinking the ask (just two data points) rather than flipping the bill into the villain ('this bill is the actual expensive, invasive thing').
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep genuinely didn't have the inversion move available and default-solved via a smaller ask, which did work procedurally.
coaching_implication: Rep could have said something like 'that bill is exactly the thing costing you $262 a month — that's the number I want to help you stop giving away,' turning the privacy fear into urgency instead of just narrowing scope.

quote: So there's no way you're not making money off me somehow.
stewart_read: Second occurrence of the trust objection, this time about profit motive; rep concedes ignorance of financials instead of reframing the utility bill as the real profiteer.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: admitting the knowledge gap builds authenticity that the customer explicitly rewards moments later ('I get the sense from you that you're not doing anything wrong').
coaching_implication: Transparency worked here for rapport, but the rep still never redirects the profit-motive suspicion toward the utility company, which was the higher-leverage reframe available.

quote: I have this weird feeling that this is gonna, like, bite people after they've signed up.
stewart_read: Third occurrence of the trust objection; rep normalizes the fear sociologically and cites a personal disqualification stat instead of reframing toward bill pain.
coaching_implication: By the third repetition the rep should recognize this as the same root objection and try a different angle (the flip) rather than another reassurance pass — this is where multi_angle_resilience should diversify strategy, not just repeat reassurance.

quote: I'm I'm gonna leave Andy out of this until I trust you.
stewart_read: Co-owner explicitly excluded by the customer; rep does not push back or attempt to include Andy on the eventual appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: pushing on Andy's inclusion here, mid-trust-crisis, likely would have collapsed the call entirely, so deferring was the safer sequencing choice.
coaching_implication: Even if deferring in the moment was right, the rep should have circled back before button-up to at least float re-including Andy once trust improved — this never happened.

quote: I don't wanna have to go mess around with your a plus rating on the better better business bureau.
stewart_read: This is a veiled threat the rep laughs off rather than addressing directly, and it lands right after she's given out her personal line for bill follow-up.
coaching_implication: Giving a personal phone number to a customer who has just threatened the company's BBB rating is a compounding privacy/security risk worth flagging for review.

quote: It will just be me from my personal line.
stewart_read: Rep gives out her personal phone number to move past the bill-privacy objection — the exact anti-pattern the schema flags for security review.
coaching_implication: This should migrate to the automated bill-capture flow once available; for now, flag for privacy/security coaching regardless of the short-term win.

quote: I don't know. I mean, I like, I'd like to be more, like, green or whatever, and I'm sure it would add value to the house.
stewart_read: This is the customer's actual interest reason (environmental + home value) delivered mid-argument; the rep does not reflect it back or use it to build forward pull.
coaching_implication: Rep should have caught this and said something like 'that's exactly the kind of thing Sam can show you the numbers on' to tie the appointment to her stated motive — instead it's filed and the conversation moves straight to cost pushback.
